key_insight: HSImul3R closes the perception–simulation gap by integrating a physics-in-the-loop, bi-directional optimization so that reconstructions from casual captures (sparse views or monocular video) are not only visually plausible but also stable and simulation-ready.
problem_solved: Existing HSI reconstruction methods produce visually plausible outputs that often violate physical constraints, causing instability or failure when used in physics engines and embodied AI tasks; HSImul3R ensures physical validity alongside visual fidelity.
method: Physics-in-the-loop, bi-directional optimization that jointly refines visual reconstruction and physical parameters to satisfy both appearance and simulation constraints.
Unified pipeline that reconstructs humans and scene geometry/interactions from sparse-view images or monocular video, with physics-aware losses and constraints.
Outputs are validated and adjusted for stability in downstream physics engines, producing simulation-ready assets for embodied AI and robotics.
impact: Provides practitioners with reliable, simulation-ready 3D human–scene interaction reconstructions from casual captures, improving robustness for embodied AI, robotics simulation, AR/VR content, and dataset generation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input (sparse images / monocular video) → perception module → physics-in-the-loop optimizer → simulation-ready output

paper_title: HSImul3R: Physics-in-the-Loop Reconstruction of Simulation-Ready Human-Scene Interactions
paper_authors: Yukang Cao, Haozhe Xie, Fangzhou Hong, Long Zhuo, Zhaoxi Chen
